title: Weather by Coordinates Context: Pin the Point
description: Pin exact coordinates for weather services with the Weather by Coordinates Context page — the lat/long pair forecast apps actually want. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a hilltop, a lake's far shore and a farm's back field share one town forecast but live three different weathers — the coordinates are how you ask about the place itself.
quick_answer: The Weather by Coordinates Context page pins the exact coordinates of a point so you can paste them into weather services that accept latitude and longitude. Find the point, copy the pair, and ask your forecast app about that spot — not the nearest town's centre, yours.
steps_intro: Forecasts are only as local as the point you give them:

faq: Which forecast model does it use?

None — this page pins coordinates for use in weather services; it does not compute a forecast. The honesty matters: forecast quality lives with the meteorological services, and this page's job is giving them your exact point.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — find any point on the map; your location is optional input, never a requirement.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Place labels around a point come from open data; weather services label their grid points independently, so names can differ while coordinates agree.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Decimal degrees (WGS84) — the format weather services accepting lat/long expect.
Why not the town name in the app?
Town-level forecasts use the town's reference point. Coordinates let the service grid your actual spot — worth it wherever terrain varies.
Go to your national weather service's warnings directly. A coordinates page is a planning convenience, never a safety source.
